name: Corsica
title: Corsica —
tagline: Napoleon's birthplace, mountains rising from the sea and a language of its own.
summary: Corsica is a mountainous island in the Mediterranean, closer to Italy than to mainland France, with its own language, polyphonic singing and strong sense of identity.

Ajaccio is the birthplace of Napoleon, Bonifacio sits on white cliffs at the south, and the GR20 is one of Europe's toughest long-distance walks. The island's cheeses, charcuterie and chestnut flour are all prized.

famous_for.title: Corsican polyphonic singing

sport.intro: SC Bastia and AC Ajaccio are the main football clubs, and Corsican derbies are passionately followed.

community.intro: Many Corsicans have served in the army and administration overseas, and large Corsican communities live in Marseille, Paris and the Americas.

ancestry: Searching for your family's roots? The French National Archives and the departmental archives hold civil registers, parish records and census returns, and many are searchable online.

fr.name: Corse
fr.eyebrow: Île de la Méditerranée · Capitale : Ajaccio
fr.title: Corse :
fr.tagline: La ville natale de Napoléon, des montagnes qui plongent dans la mer et une langue bien à elle.
summary: La Corse est une île montagneuse de la Méditerranée, plus proche de l'Italie que de la France continentale, avec sa propre langue, ses chants polyphoniques et un fort sentiment d'identité.

Ajaccio est la ville natale de Napoléon, Bonifacio se dresse sur des falaises blanches au sud, et le GR20 est l'un des sentiers de grande randonnée les plus difficiles d'Europe. Les fromages, la charcuterie et la farine de châtaigne de l'île sont très appréciés.
